sections.h2: What kind of place is Parkland, and how does that shape a sale?
sections.html:
Parkland sits in the northwest corner of Broward County, and its buyers tend to want acreage, quiet streets and newer construction. The city describes itself as stretching west from State Road 7 to the Everglades and north from the Sawgrass Expressway to Loxahatchee Road.

Parkland was founded in 1963 by a cattle farmer who bought more than 1,000 acres of Everglades land with his father and parceled out plots from his ranch. Early buyers could get five acres for as little as $15,000. Roads stayed unpaved until the 1980s and the first traffic light did not arrive until the 1990s, which explains why parts of the city still feel rural. The city says it grew from under 100 residents and 420 acres to nearly 38,000 residents and more than 8,000 acres.

For a seller, that history matters in practical ways. Many lots are large, some properties sit on equestrian or trail corridors, and the age and style of homes vary a lot from one neighborhood to the next. Buyers who pay cash often care less about finishes and more about roof, drainage and permit history, so pull your records before you talk to anyone.

sections.h2: Which sale routes fit a Parkland owner?
sections.html:
Three routes exist for a Parkland owner: a brokered listing, a private sale, or a direct cash purchase. Time and repair budget usually decide among them.

  • Brokered listing: the widest buyer pool, with prep work, showings and a wait on the buyer's financing.
  • Private sale: you skip the commission but handle pricing, contract and disclosures yourself.
  • Direct cash purchase: quicker and as-is, with the price reflecting repair and resale risk.

Compare offers on what you actually net after repairs, taxes, fees and carrying costs, and read any contract before you sign. A Parkland house with a newer roof and clean permits will draw stronger bids on every route.

sections.h2: Who issues building permits in Parkland, and how does that touch a sale?
sections.html:
The city's Building Department at 6600 University Drive issues permits and certificates of occupancy, and its phone line is 954.753.5447. The department lists weekday office hours on its page, Monday through Thursday from 7:00 AM to 6:00 PM.

The city moved permitting to a new online portal, and the page tells contractors to re-register and submit fresh insurance and license documents. Permit fees were adjusted beginning October 1, 2025 under a city resolution, so ask the department for the current schedule if you plan repairs before selling.

Open or expired permits on past roof, window or addition work can slow a closing. Ask the Building Department what is on record for your address before you list.

sections.h2: How do Florida property taxes work for a Parkland seller?
sections.html:
Broward County bills the tax and the state sets the calendar. Florida values property as of January 1, owners file exemptions by March 1, and tax bills go out in November.

  • Early payment discounts run 4 percent in November, 3 percent in December, 2 percent in January and 1 percent in February.
  • Unpaid taxes turn delinquent on April 1.
  • A homestead exemption of up to $50,000 applies when the home is your permanent residence on January 1.

A sale resets the assessed value to just value the next January 1, so the buyer's bill can be much higher than yours. That is why a long-time owner's tax figure is a poor guide for a buyer. The Broward appraiser's office lists 954-357-6830 and weekday hours of 8 am to 5 pm.

sections.h2: What does the state charge to transfer a deed?
sections.html:
Florida charges documentary stamp tax on deeds, and Broward County uses the standard statewide rate. Every party to the document is liable, whichever side agrees to pay.

Florida deed and recording charges as printed by the state
ItemRate as printedSource
Deed doc stamps70 cents per $100 of considerationFla. Stat. 201.02
Mortgage doc stamps35 cents per $100 securedDOR page
Clerk recording, first page$5.00, then $4.00 per added pageFla. Stat. 28.24
Added names beyond four$1.00 eachFla. Stat. 28.24

The clerk collects the tax at recording. Ask your closing agent for a written estimate that applies these rates to your price.

sections.h2: What if the Parkland house is inherited or behind on payments?
sections.html:
Both situations have fixed court steps in Florida. For an estate, summary administration is open when the non-exempt estate is $150,000 or less, or when the owner died more than two years ago.

In a foreclosure, the final judgment sets a public sale between 20 and 35 days later unless the lender agrees to longer. The winning bidder posts a 5 percent deposit, and homestead owners should check with the clerk within 10 days of the sale about any surplus. Selling before the sale date can protect equity, so talk to a Florida attorney and your lender early.

  • Gather the deed, recent tax bill and any lender letters.
  • Ask the Broward clerk what is filed against the property.
  • Get a payoff statement before you compare offers.

sections.h2: What happens if property taxes go unpaid on a Parkland house?
sections.html:
Unpaid taxes turn delinquent on April 1, and tax certificates are sold on unpaid items by June 1. A certificate holder may file for a tax deed once two years have passed since April 1 of the issue year, with an application fee of $75.

The tax collector then lists the people who must be noticed, including the titleholder, lienholders and any contract for deed buyer. If you are behind, selling before a deed application is filed keeps options open. Ask the Broward tax collector for a payoff figure.

  • Homestead owners over 65 may be able to defer part of the bill with Form DR-570 by March 31.
  • Installment prepayment requires an application by May 1.
  • Partial payments are at the collector's discretion.

sections.h2: Can an unlisted family transfer or quitclaim help me sell in Parkland?
sections.html:
A quitclaim is a taxable document under the DOR list, and it counts as a change of ownership for Save Our Homes unless an exception such as a spouse transfer applies. A transfer to a relative before sale can raise the property's tax base and add stamp tax.

A lady bird deed has its own treatment under a DOR advisement, which says it does not transfer a present beneficial interest on the facts presented. Talk to an attorney before recording anything.

sections.h2: What about tenants in a Parkland rental?
sections.html:
Florida lets a landlord end a tenancy on nonpayment with a 3 day written notice that excludes weekends and court holidays. For a curable lease breach the tenant gets 7 days to fix it.

Month-to-month tenancies end with at least 30 days' notice. If you plan to sell a tenant-occupied home, read the lease first, since a sale does not automatically end it. A buyer who wants vacant possession will price the delay.

faqs.q: Who sets the property tax calendar for a Parkland home?
faqs.a: The state sets the calendar and Broward County officials apply it. Values are fixed as of January 1, exemption filings are due March 1, bills arrive in November and unpaid taxes go delinquent April 1.

faqs.q: Does a cash sale in Parkland avoid doc stamp tax?
faqs.a: No. Florida taxes deeds at 70 cents per $100 of consideration on the DOR page, and all parties to the document are liable whoever agrees to pay. Settle who pays in the contract.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Parkland house with open permits?
faqs.a: Yes, but expect friction. Ask the city Building Department at 954.753.5447 what is open on your address, because buyers and title companies will find it anyway.

faqs.q: What happens to my homestead exemption when I sell?
faqs.a: It ends with your ownership. Homestead is lost when the home stops being your permanent residence, and the buyer's assessment resets to just value the following January 1.

faqs.q: How soon can an inherited Parkland house be sold?
faqs.a: It depends on the court path. Summary administration is available for non-exempt estates up to $150,000, and larger or contested estates take formal administration, so speak with a probate attorney.
